title: Fourier formula for noise stability
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, correlation parameter $\rho\in[0,1]$, and function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the noise stability of $f$ equals $\sum_a \rho^{|\operatorname{supp}(a)|}\widehat f(a)^2$, summed over all multi-indices $a$, where $\operatorname{supp}(a)$ consists of the coordinates at which $a$ differs from the distinguished constant-basis index, and $\widehat f(a)$ is the corresponding Fourier coefficient.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$B$ is a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ containing the constant-one function
